scenes.headline: DBU Cost Management
scenes.subtitle: Get more work done per dollar
scenes.narration: DBU cost management tunes clusters and workloads so you pay only for the compute you truly need.

scenes.headline: How Databricks billing works
items: A DBU is a unit of processing consumed per second
Total cost = DBUs (Databricks) + cloud VM cost
Rate varies by workload tier and Photon usage
scenes.narration: Databricks bills in DBUs, a normalized measure of processing over time. Your bill combines DBU charges with the underlying cloud VM cost. The DBU rate depends on the workload type and whether Photon is enabled.

scenes.headline: Levers to reduce cost
items: Use spot instances for fault-tolerant jobs
Right-size instance types to the workload
Prefer job clusters over always-on clusters
scenes.narration: Autoscaling matches capacity to demand while auto-termination kills idle clusters. Spot instances cut VM cost sharply for resilient workloads. Right-sizing avoids overpaying for unused memory or cores, and ephemeral job clusters stop billing the moment work finishes.

scenes.headline: All-purpose vs job clusters
scenes.narration: All-purpose clusters suit interactive development but carry a higher rate and often sit idle. Job clusters spin up for a run and terminate immediately after, at a lower rate. Moving scheduled production work to job clusters is one of the biggest wins.

scenes.headline: Monitor and attribute spend
items: Tag clusters for chargeback by team
Watch system tables for usage trends
scenes.narration: Cluster tags let you attribute cost back to teams and projects. Billing system tables reveal usage patterns and waste over time. Budget alerts catch runaway spend before it becomes a surprise.

scenes.text: Autoscale, auto-terminate, use spot and job clusters, and tag everything.
scenes.narration: The cheapest DBU is the one you never spin up on idle compute.
